newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seita sees satisfactory '97 oper profit.
newsitem.headline: Seita sees satisfactory '97 oper profit.

text.p: French tobacco company Seita should post "satisfactory" operating profit this year despite losing market share to lower priced products, Seita chairman Jean-Dominique Comolli said on Tuesday.

"Significant corrective measures have been taken to allow us to maintain satisfactory operating profit," he told an annual shareholders' meeting. The moves include cutting operating costs and boosting productivity.
In 1996, Seita, best known for its pungent Gauloises and Gitanes cigarettes, posted operating profit of 1.24 billion francs. Net attributable profit rose in 1996 by 15 percent to 786 million francs.
Comolli warned of an "elevated risk of an all-out price war in the French market", noting that some manufacturers had submitted proposals to the state to cut prices.
But he said Seita hoped the government would seek to avert such an event. "I do not despair a reasonable solution for all parties concerned, notably for Seita, can be found," he said.
But Comolli said Seita was ready to meet the challenge if a price war erupts. "If there has to be a price war, Seita will reposition itself in a fashion to reconquer the consumer," he said.
Plans for price cuts must be submitted to the finance ministry for authorisation. The ministry's decision has been delayed by a snap two-round parliamentary election called for May 25 and June 1.
Seita's market share of blonde cigarette sales in which competition is intense fell to 18 percent in the first quarter of 1997 from 20.5 percent a year earlier.
